title: A walk can click the history bar and film its filter moving
goal: Scripted walks cannot click anything in the history bar, so nobody can prove by a walk that its All / Screenshots / Videos filter moves like every other segmented control, or that its buttons work. Make a walk able to press the history bar the way a pointer does, then film the filter moving.
notes: Reproduced 2026-09-29 while doing every-segmented-control-is-the-one-system-glass. With the history window added to PlaytestHarness.panelWindows() (the harness only looks in the editor, its children, sheets and Settings), a press step found "Videos" and clicked it: note "\"Videos\" in tooltip none at window (891, 174), one click; ... no view bodies counted", and the snapshot after still showed the thumb on All with the capture still listed. Giving the history panel a hosting view with acceptsFirstMouse true changed nothing. Likely cause: a walk never lets the history panel (HistoryOverlayPanel, nonactivating, canBecomeKey true) become key (AppFront.showFloating), so the mouse-down is spent making it key; the menu-picture path works round it by making the strip key for one second (PlaytestHarness ~9947). The harness change and the acceptsFirstMouse try were both reverted. A person is not affected: their strip is key when it opens.
acceptance: A walk step presses Videos in the history bar at a point on its face and the filter changes to Videos
segmented-thumb-film-walk films the history filter All to Videos and back with filmThumb, inside its rail in every frame
focus-drill reads clean for that walk

log.note: 2026-09-29: the history filter is now the Mac's own segmented control (every-segmented-control-is-apple-s-own-liquid-gl). There is no drawn thumb to film; what is left is proving a click on the filter and on the bar's buttons works.

below the follow-up bar: the drawn thumb it would have filmed is gone (the filter is the system control now), and what is left is a walk tooling gap nobody using the app sees. Folded into every-segmented-control-is-apple-s-own-liquid-gl's log.
